clue.text: Model that I own in no sense

indicators.note: to model is to shape or form, so the following words are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone disowns a model, insisting it is not theirs in any way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal: the letters of THAT I OWN are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean not at all, a whit being the tiniest amount.

clue.text: I'm surprised it's expressed poetically for US inventor

parts.note: O is an exclamation of surprise
'tis is the poetic contraction of it is

explanation.surface: An exclamation and an old-fashioned phrase are offered as a tribute to an American inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Elisha Otis invented the safety lift (elevator).
explanation.definitionFit: Elisha Otis was the American who devised the safety elevator brake.

clue.text: Time passed with more security overlooking a handover

parts.note: ran, as time ran or passed

indicators.note: overlooking means leaving something out, so the letter a is dropped

parts.note: safer means with more security
taken as written

explanation.surface: A security-conscious handover of something, with time passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooking a' removes the A from SAFER, leaving SFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfer is the passing of something from one party to another, which is a handover.

clue.text: House of Lords having nothing from sell-offs? That'll show this Tory member

indicators.note: the phrase says the first words keep none of the letters found in the following word

parts.note: the letters S, E, L, O and F that make up this word, struck out wherever they appear

explanation.surface: A peer in the House of Lords is linked to privatisation sell-offs.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike every S, E, L, O and F from HOUSE OF LORDS and only H, U, R, D survive. Douglas Hurd was a Conservative cabinet minister, later a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Hurd was a senior Conservative politician, Home and Foreign Secretary under Thatcher and Major.

clue.text: Successfully applied pressure to smoke pipe in pub; overturned last month

indicators.note: in places the smoke pipe within the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a flue carries smoke from a fire

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means the abbreviation is read upwards

parts.note: December, abbreviated DEC, is the last month of the year

explanation.surface: Someone smokes a pipe in a pub and ends up being sick, last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' reverses DEC to CED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have influenced someone is to have swayed them by pressure that worked.

clue.text: Endlessly disobedient 1

definitions.note: refers to 1 Down, meaning not at all

indicators.note: without its end means the last letter of the word for disobedient is lost

parts.note: naughty means disobedient

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about a child who is constantly disobedient.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 1 points to the solution of 1 Down as the definition; 'Endlessly' cuts the last letter from NAUGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Naught means nothing, and 1 Down means in no way at all, so both express zero.

clue.text: Venerable lady stigmatised, losing crown in contest

indicators.note: in places the shortened word inside the word for contest

parts.note: a game is a contest

indicators.note: in a down clue the crown is the top, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to be branded is to be stigmatised

explanation.surface: An elderly lady is disgraced after losing a title in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing crown' removes the B from BRANDED, leaving RANDED, which goes 'in' GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A grande dame is an elderly, dignified and influential woman.

clue.text: Opening numbers dropped from libretto about vessel in battle scene

indicators.note: about means turned round, so what is left is read backwards
the opening letters L and I are both Roman numerals, and they are removed

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An opera libretto about a ship, set in a battle scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping LI (L=50, I=1) leaves BRETTO, which 'about' turns into OTTERB. The Battle of Otterburn (1388) was fought between Scots and English in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Otterburn is the Northumberland site of a famous Anglo-Scottish battle of 1388.

clue.text: What's seen at start of any road running one way?

definitions.text: What's seen at start of any road running one way?

indicators.note: at the start of each following word, the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A question about the sign at the entrance to a one-way street.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of 'any road running one way' spell the answer, and the whole clue describes the sign at the start of a one-way street.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way street is marked by a sign showing a pointer in the permitted direction of travel.

clue.text: Minute: 1,000 or 10,080 of them

parts.note: wee means tiny, the adjective minute
K stands for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how many minutes there are in various spans of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like a noun (sixty seconds) but is the adjective meaning tiny; yet it also feeds the definition, since 10,080 minutes make seven days.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven days of 1,440 minutes each total 10,080 minutes.

clue.text: Before this crime we would make passes tediously

indicators.note: the word we placed before the solution would make the phrase meaning passes tediously

parts.note: time that wears on drags by slowly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tediously making passes before committing a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Put WE in front of the solution and you get WEARS ON, which means passes tediously.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Investigator with authorisation's good for carbon industry

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police investigator

indicators.note: G (good) takes the place of C (carbon), the chemical symbol

parts.note: a licence is an authorisation

explanation.surface: A detective with a permit for good work in the carbon industry.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first C of LICENCE is replaced, giving LIGENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry in the sense of hard work and diligence is steady, careful effort.

clue.text: Wife leaving exotic flower'll put in low shrub swiftly

indicators.note: put in places the rearranged letters inside the shrub

parts.note: heather is a low-growing shrub

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange, so the letters are rearranged
the letter for wife leaves, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A wife departs as exotic flowers are swiftly planted among heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the seven letters left after the wife goes, and 'put in' places them after the first letter of the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at breakneck speed is an idiom for travelling as fast as possible.

clue.text: People involved with deeds that crash office computer networks?

parts.note: a LAN is a local area network, as used in an office
downers here are whatever brings a network down

explanation.surface: Hackers whose actions bring down an office's computer networks.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the answer as 'LAN-downers', things that take local networks down.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners of land hold title deeds to their property.

clue.text: One with tales to tell of deception in tax application

indicators.note: in places the deception inside the tax

parts.note: a rate is a tax
a con is a deception
use is an application

explanation.surface: Someone with a story to tell about a fraudulent tax claim.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE is a local property tax in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteuse is a female storyteller.

clue.text: Mostly, John Brown leads with ritual and meditation?

indicators.note: leads means the colour comes first

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a john or a trick is a prostitute's client, both American slang

explanation.surface: A man called John Brown leads a session of ritual and meditation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John Brown' looks like a name but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric practice in Hindu and Buddhist traditions uses ritual, mantra and meditation.

clue.text: After turnover, blast that kind of unfinished dessert

indicators.note: turned over means the whole sequence is read backwards

parts.note: drat and blast are both mild oaths

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: such means that kind

explanation.surface: Someone curses after a pastry turnover goes wrong and a dessert is left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' looks like the pastry, but 'After turnover' reverses the whole run, giving CUSTARD from the oath plus the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet egg-and-milk sauce or pudding served as a dessert.

clue.text: Society leaving out someone having 5 victims?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of leaving are disordered

explanation.surface: A society drops a person who has claimed five victims.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to 5 Down: Svengali, from George du Maurier's novel Trilby, controls people by hypnosis, so his victims are influenced.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali is the hypnotist of du Maurier's Trilby, whose name means one who manipulates others.

clue.text: Female in seedy premises left untidy

indicators.note: in places the female inside the seedy premises

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club
she refers to a female

explanation.surface: A woman in a run-down bar who has left looking untidy.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishevel is to make hair or clothing messy, a verb like the definition.

clue.text: See leaf ridges covering wild linseed plant

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: covering means the veins go round the scrambled letters

parts.note: veins are the ridges on a leaf

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of linseed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Botanical instructions to look at the veins on the leaf of a wild linseed plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns LINSEED into IDLENES, which VEINS covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-in-idleness is an old name for the wild pansy, the flower used in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Beguile flustered parent

indicators.note: flustered means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent gets flustered by a sweet-talking child.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or trick someone into a trap.

clue.text: Bad press has Columbo actor's guts churning

indicators.note: the guts are the middle letters, which are turned round

parts.note: Peter Falk played the TV detective Columbo

explanation.surface: Critics attack, leaving the actor who played Columbo feeling sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle letters AL of FALK reverse, giving LA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is harsh criticism, as from the press.

clue.text: In municipality near Mons, Ghent unexpectedly extends

indicators.note: in places the scrambled city inside the town name

parts.note: Lens is a small municipality in Hainaut, Belgium, near Mons

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters of Ghent are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Belgian travel note about Ghent unexpectedly spreading near Mons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges the Belgian city's name into GTHEN, and 'In' sets it inside the little Hainaut town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To lengthen something is to make it longer, which is to extend it.

clue.text: Little time to gather in parking requirements

indicators.note: to gather in means the short time wraps round the letter

parts.note: sec is short for second, a little time
P is the symbol for parking

explanation.surface: There is little time to collect requirements for parking.
explanation.definitionFit: A spec, short for specification, sets out what is needed.

clue.text: Brush or pasture

explanation.surface: A choice between two activities involving grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Graze means a light touch or scrape, and also to feed on grass or put animals out to feed.

clue.text: Stretch of land like Iowa

parts.note: as means like
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A comparison of a stretch of land with the US state of Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is a continent, the largest landmass on Earth.

clue.text: Suffering periodic losses, retiring farmer lacks system for reaping what's sown

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the letters are read in reverse
losing letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter

explanation.surface: A struggling farmer about to retire has no way to harvest his crops.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of FARMER LACKS give AMRAK, which 'retiring' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma is the belief that one's deeds return to one, as the saying about reaping what you sow puts it.

clue.text: Lug 50 litres aboard the ship with relish

parts.note: a ship is traditionally referred to as she
L is the Roman numeral for 50
to relish something is to like it

explanation.surface: A sailor carries fifty litres of drink on board and enjoys it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' looks like a verb (carry) but is British slang for the ear; shell-like is a jokey term for ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shell-like is British colloquial for an ear, from its curved shape.
